clue.text: React with amazement and shoot the sequence twice

definitions.meaning: to look again in sudden surprise at something only half-noticed at first
in film-making, to film the same scene a second time, i.e. take it two times

explanation.surface: A film director, astonished, orders the scene to be filmed again.
explanation.definitionFit: A delayed second look of surprise is the idiom; read literally it means performing a filmed take twice.

clue.text: I enter to pass judgment on god's murderer

indicators.note: the letter I is told to go into the verb, so it is placed inside it

parts.note: to pass judgment is to decide

explanation.surface: A judge steps in to rule on someone accused of killing a deity.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun names one who kills a divine being, from Latin deus plus the killing suffix.

clue.text: Embarrassing drawback after a week

indicators.note: the drawback piece is set to come behind the a-plus-week pieces

parts.note: the word draw turned back gives these letters

explanation.surface: An awkward downside crops up after seven days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawback' reads as one noun, a downside, but the setter splits it: the word draw, then 'back' telling you to read it backwards, joined 'after' the opening pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe a situation causing discomfort or social unease; a close synonym.

clue.text: Computer units described by educational journal

parts.note: TES is the Times Educational Supplement, a British teachers' weekly

explanation.surface: Information about computer memory appears in a teaching magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: The TES (Times Educational Supplement) is a British weekly paper for teachers.
explanation.definitionFit: Each is a group of eight bits, a standard measure of digital storage.

clue.text: Tim goes mad as a result of self-glorification

indicators.note: mad suggests the letters of Tim goes have gone crazy and are jumbled

explanation.surface: A man called Tim goes crazy because of his own vanity.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive self-regard and boasting about oneself; a close synonym.

clue.text: Car rug from the vending-machine

parts.note: auto is a common short word for a car
a mat is a small rug

explanation.surface: A travel blanket bought from a coin-operated dispenser.
explanation.definitionFit: An early coin-operated food dispenser or the self-service cafe built around one; an example of the term.

clue.text: Take up a challenge to catalogue

definitions.meaning: originally to ride into the jousting arena, so to accept a contest
read literally, to put an item into the inventories or registers

explanation.surface: Accepting a dare means writing down an inventory.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from tournaments' fenced arenas; read literally it means adding items to registers.

clue.text: Persevere, but get small credit

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
on tick is British slang for on credit

explanation.surface: Keep going, even if the loan offered is meagre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tick' is British slang for credit, as in buying something 'on tick'.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep at something, as in sticking with a task; a phrasal synonym.

clue.text: No public worship for government agents

definitions.meaning: a religious rite held in private, read literally

explanation.surface: Spies for the state hold their prayers in private.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of covert state intelligence bodies; read literally, a church rite held privately.

clue.text: Cheap clothing acquires a little bird-fair exchange

definitions.text: Cheap clothing acquires a little bird
definitions.meaning: tat is cheap clothing, and here it is bought in return for a tit, a small bird

explanation.surface: Trading a small songbird for some shoddy garments seems an even swap.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is cryptic: cheap stuff (TAT) obtained in exchange for a small bird (TIT), a swap of one for the other.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means retaliating in kind, an equal return of blows or favours.

clue.text: Slut offers work to a goblin

indicators.note: the work piece is attached to the goblin, so it comes after it

parts.note: a troll is a goblin-like creature of folklore
op, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: An insult traded while handing out jobs to a mythical creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'offers work to' means the work (OP, short for opus) is added after the goblin.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are old, derogatory words for a promiscuous or slovenly woman.

clue.text: Where gangsters had to be smart in the past

parts.note: chic means stylish or smart
ago means in the past, as in years ago

explanation.surface: Mobsters in former days had to look well dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: The US city was famous for Prohibition-era gangsters such as Al Capone.
explanation.definitionFit: This city is the classic setting for 1920s mobsters and bootleggers; a cryptic description.

clue.text: One who carries increasingly little weight

definitions.text: One who carries increasingly little weight

parts.words: One who carries increasingly little weight
parts.note: read as a person losing weight, or as a comparative adjective for something getting thinner

explanation.surface: Someone whose importance keeps shrinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A dieter sheds pounds over time, carrying less body weight each week.

clue.text: Revise part of the score Mendelssohn wrote

indicators.note: part of says only a portion of the words score Mendelssohn is taken

explanation.surface: An editor amends a passage of a composer's manuscript.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct or improve a text; a close synonym.

clue.text: No goals scored in a happy marriage

definitions.meaning: love is zero in tennis scoring, so a contest where nobody scores
a union made for affection rather than money

explanation.surface: A goalless draw is likened to a contented wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedding made for affection; read literally, a contest with a nil scoreline, love meaning zero.

clue.text: Tripper makes retired cleric embrace strange form of yoga

indicators.note: the cleric piece wraps round the reworked yoga letters
retired means going back, so the cleric's letters are read backwards

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a title for a cleric

indicators.note: a strange form of the word yoga means its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A retired vicar takes up an odd type of yoga on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' and 'strange form of' each work on the word beside them, and 'embrace' then wraps the turned cleric round the jumbled yoga. A tripper here is a traveller, not someone who stumbles.
explanation.definitionFit: A tripper is a traveller on a journey, and this word means one making a long journey.

clue.text: Punch-drunk, but quite unconcerned

definitions.meaning: dazed from repeated blows, like a battered boxer
carefree to the point of being reckless

explanation.surface: A dazed boxer who seems not to care.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally dazed from blows; figuratively happy-go-lucky and casual.

clue.text: Identity badge for a group of marines

parts.note: RM stands for Royal Marines
a band is a group of people

explanation.surface: A soldier's sleeve insignia worn by a troop of seaborne soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: RM stands for the Royal Marines, Britain's naval infantry.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of cloth worn on the upper sleeve to show role or affiliation; an example.

clue.text: Forestall the Red Queen's oft-repeated sentence

definitions.meaning: the Queen in Alice keeps shouting 'Off with his head!', a sentence of beheading

explanation.surface: Anticipating a royal figure's catchphrase in a famous story.
explanation.walkthrough: In Lewis Carroll's Alice books the furious Queen constantly orders beheadings ('Off with her head!'); Carroll's shouting queen is strictly the Queen of Hearts.
explanation.definitionFit: To block or intercept beforehand; read literally, a beheading order.

clue.text: Female to complain bitterly if lacking strength

parts.note: to rail is to protest angrily

explanation.surface: A woman grumbles when her energy fails.
explanation.definitionFit: Weak or delicate in body; a close synonym.

clue.text: Body of farmers returned just for the entertainment

indicators.note: returned means the farmers' body letters are turned round

parts.note: the setter takes NUF as an initialism for a national union of farmers
just means fair and even-handed

explanation.surface: A farming union came back purely to enjoy itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns NUF round. Britain's farmers' union is usually the NFU, so the setter's NUF is a stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: A travelling show with rides and stalls is a form of amusement; an example.

clue.text: A time to get amphetamine-and fast

parts.note: speed is slang for amphetamine

explanation.surface: Someone takes stimulants and moves rapidly.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving quickly; the phrase is an adverbial synonym.

clue.text: Beat down a section of the embankment

parts.note: to ram is to pound or force down
a part is a section of something

explanation.surface: A stretch of riverbank is being hammered flat.
explanation.definitionFit: A defensive wall of earth or a raised bank; an example of an embankment.

clue.text: Fish net sent back by an honourable man

indicators.note: sent back means the letters of net are reversed

parts.note: taken as the word itself
CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A respectable gentleman returns a fishing net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' turns NET into TEN. CH is a Companion of Honour, a British award.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshwater carp species is a type of fish; an example.

clue.text: The origin is reflected in hereditary factors

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the hereditary-factors word

parts.note: genes are the units of heredity

indicators.note: reflected as in a mirror means the word is is read backwards

explanation.surface: Where we come from shows in our inherited traits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' turns IS into SI, which goes 'in' GENES.
explanation.definitionFit: Means the beginning or coming into being, also the Bible's opening book.

clue.text: Where little Jack sat up against a wall

definitions.text: Where little Jack sat up against a wall

parts.words: Where little Jack sat up against a wall
parts.note: recalls the nursery rhyme about Jack Horner, and also a position with nowhere left to go

explanation.surface: A nursery-rhyme boy sitting by a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme 'Little Jack Horner' begins with him sitting in an angle of a room eating pie.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Horner's seat in the rhyme; also an idiom for being trapped with no escape.

clue.text: Offers to help find Lincoln back-street

parts.note: Abe was US President Abraham Lincoln's nickname

indicators.note: back means the street abbreviation is read backwards

explanation.surface: Looking for a lane behind the houses in an English city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back-street' looks like a single word, but 'back' is the reversal signal working on street. Lincoln is the US president, not the English city.
explanation.definitionFit: To encourage or assist someone, often in wrongdoing; a close synonym.

clue.text: The aim of all nations when Armageddon comes

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal
belonging to the whole globe, the world's nations together

explanation.surface: Every country hopes for something when the final battle arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: In scripture this final battle signals the close of earthly existence; a synonym for doomsday.
